Octagon: put a=(1+sqrt(2))/2 and b=1/2. The ideal flat-oriented regular octagon has vertices(+-a,+-b),(+-b,+-a), with |x|,|y|<=a and |x+y|,|x-y|<=a+b. Define the column step h=(3+sqrt(2))/2 and full vertical period v=2a=1+sqrt(2). The owner centers are(h*i,v*j+a*(i mod2)). Owners in one column separate by the horizontal face normal. In neighboring columns their minimal vertical offset is a, and h+a=2(a+b), so a diagonal face normal separates them. Columns two or more apart separate on x since2h>2a. Thus these whole octagons form the classical dense staggered lattice. This is the standard face-contact lattice seen after its forced45-degree symmetry change, not a tuned angle.

Dodecagon: put a=(2+sqrt(3))/2, v=2a and h=sqrt(3)*a=(3+2sqrt(3))/2. The ideal flat-oriented regular dodecagon has apothem a and support normals at integer multiples of30degrees. Use centers(h*i,v*j+a*(i mod2)). One-column pairs separate on y. Neighboring columns at the minimal offset a separate along the30-degree face normal because (sqrt(3)/2)*h+a/2=2a. More distant columns separate on x because2h>2a. These are complete dodecagons in the standard triangular face-contact lattice. The column direction is forced by those face contacts.

For either source, a c-column by r-row patch consists of every whole owner with0<=i<c,0<=j<r. Its exact bounding box dimensions are(v+(c-1)*h,v*r+epsilon*v/2,L), epsilon=1 if c>1 and0 otherwise. Its midpoint is((c-1)*h/2,(r-1)*v/2+epsilon*v/4,0). Both side costs and the unmatched staggered end are retained. The ideal owner frame is fixed at pi/8 for the octagon or pi/12 for the dodecagon relative to the canonical source. No angle is searched.

Layers concatenate with their full thicknesses. Keep each proper axis-permutation quaternion and act on the whole patch, including every owner frame. The full backpointer word is an inverse decoder. Distinct boxes have disjoint interiors, and every within-patch pair has the source separator just proved. A named suffix of whole owners may be deleted while retaining its complete parent.
